question.text: Which of the following individual investors meets SEBI's Accredited Investor (AI) eligibility criteria?

answer.text: Annual income of INR 1.5 crore only, no other disclosures
Net worth of INR 5 crore (none in financial assets)
Annual income of INR 50 lakh and net worth of INR 7.5 crore of which INR 2 crore is financial assets

explanation.text: The Logic: For individuals (and HUF, Family Trust, Sole Prop, Partnership), AI eligibility is met by ANY of: (a) income ≥ INR 2 cr; OR (b) net worth ≥ INR 7.5 cr with ≥ INR 3.75 cr in financial assets; OR (c) income ≥ INR 1 cr AND net worth ≥ INR 5 cr with ≥ INR 2.5 cr in financial assets. Primary residence excluded from net worth. The Trap: Option A is income INR 1.5 cr alone — below INR 2 cr standalone and no net-worth support. Option C lacks financial-asset composition. Option D has INR 2 cr financial assets but criterion (c) requires INR 2.5 cr. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B, XIX-C all test the same matrix. XIX-E cares about the INR 50 cr body-corporate threshold most and individual thresholds for cross-check. Manager's Pro-Tip: When marketing an LVF or AI-only scheme, pre-screen prospects with a quick three-criteria check. Primary residence carve-out often is the tipping factor — clarify upfront.
